title: Prostate cancer: why ADT, when to intensify, and where radiotherapy fits
review_status: Draft educational content; independent oncology and pharmacy review pending
intro: Treatment depends on two separate questions: where is the cancer, and is it progressing despite a castrate testosterone level? A rising PSA alone does not identify the correct treatment. Establish stage, PSA kinetics, testosterone, symptoms, previous treatment and the patient’s goals.
boundary: This educational overview explains treatment choices. It does not select a regimen or change SACTCheck eligibility, dose or treatment-status rules. Guideline evidence, an EMA licence and an NCCP funded indication are separate checks. Verify the current Irish prescribing and reimbursement route for the exact setting.

sections.title: What each treatment does
paragraphs: Most prostate adenocarcinomas use androgen receptor signalling to grow. Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) reduces testicular testosterone. GnRH agonists, such as leuprorelin, initially stimulate and then suppress pituitary signalling; antagonists, such as degarelix or relugolix, block it directly without the initial testosterone flare. Orchiectomy achieves permanent testicular androgen suppression.

An androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) adds a different level of blockade. Abiraterone is an ARPI: it inhibits CYP17-mediated androgen synthesis, including production outside the testes. Enzalutamide, apalutamide and darolutamide act at the androgen receptor. They are alternatives selected for a particular setting, not a routine four-drug combination.

Abiraterone also reduces cortisol synthesis. Increased ACTH drive can cause mineralocorticoid excess: hypertension, low potassium and fluid retention. Prescribed prednisolone suppresses this drive. NCCP 00577 uses 5 mg daily for mHSPC; 00103 uses 10 mg daily, or 5 mg twice daily, for mCRPC. Do not interchange these schedules or stop the steroid abruptly without a plan.

Castration resistance means progression despite castrate testosterone; it does not mean androgen signalling is irrelevant. Continue medical ADT in these five NCCP regimens unless the patient has had surgical castration. Confirm testosterone suppression and adherence when assessing progression.

sections.title: When ADT and additional treatment are used
rows: Localised, favourable-risk disease
Active surveillance or a local treatment may be appropriate. ADT is not a universal treatment for every prostate cancer diagnosis.
Radiotherapy can be definitive local treatment; whether to add ADT depends on the risk group.
Unfavourable intermediate-risk or high-risk localised / locally advanced disease
ADT can accompany radical radiotherapy. NICE recommends 6 months for CPG 2–5 and consideration of up to 3 years for CPG 4–5; the radiation oncology plan specifies duration.
The aim may be cure. Selected high-risk nonmetastatic patients also benefit from abiraterone-based intensification; this is broader evidence, not an extension of the metastatic NCCP 00577 entry.
Biochemical recurrence after surgery or radiotherapy
Review PSA doubling time, imaging, prior local therapy and suitability for salvage. A PSA rise does not automatically require lifelong ADT.
Early salvage radiotherapy after prostatectomy may still be curative. Selected high-risk recurrence can justify systemic intensification; EMBARK is a distinct population, not nmCRPC.
Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC)

Discuss ADT plus an ARPI upfront in suitable patients. Waiting for ADT failure is not the default. Chemotherapy fitness and disease pattern inform whether a docetaxel-containing triplet is appropriate.
Consider prostate radiotherapy for newly diagnosed, low-volume metastatic disease. It complements systemic treatment.
Nonmetastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC)
For high-risk disease, usually PSA doubling time ≤10 months, add an indicated AR inhibitor while continuing ADT. Establish progression despite castrate testosterone.
Pivotal trials defined nonmetastatic disease using conventional imaging. A PSMA PET finding needs multidisciplinary interpretation; it does not automatically reproduce a trial category.
Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC)

Continue ADT. Choose the next treatment using prior ARPI/chemotherapy exposure, symptoms, disease distribution and molecular results. Sequential ARPIs may have limited benefit because of cross-resistance.
Radiotherapy can relieve pain or local symptoms. Consider chemotherapy, biomarker-selected targeted therapy or radioligand treatment where indicated and available.

sections.title: Choosing intensification for the person in front of you
paragraphs: Abiraterone: review cardiovascular disease, blood pressure, potassium, oedema, liver function, diabetes, steroid suitability and fasting instructions. Its monitoring and steroid burden differ from the receptor inhibitors.

Enzalutamide: review fatigue, cognition, falls and fracture risk, seizure predisposition, blood pressure and interactions. It can reduce exposure to other medicines through enzyme induction. A pharmacist should check anticoagulants and every prescription, supplement and herbal product.

Apalutamide: review rash and severe skin reactions, thyroid function, falls/fractures, seizure and cardiovascular history, interactions and new pulmonary symptoms. Use the current NCCP version 5, reviewed 1 July 2026, rather than the superseded version 4.

Darolutamide: assess kidney and liver function, cardiovascular history and interactions, including transporter-related statin interactions. A different interaction and CNS profile does not make it risk-free. The patient must be able to follow twice-daily dosing with food.

Docetaxel adds cytotoxic treatment and a different burden: marrow suppression, infection, neuropathy and infusion visits. ARASENS tested adding darolutamide to ADT plus docetaxel; it did not directly prove that triplet therapy is better than ADT plus an ARPI. Do not rank drugs by comparing hazard ratios from separate trials.

sections.title: Radiotherapy has several different jobs
paragraphs: CHAARTED high volume means visceral metastases or at least four bone metastases, with at least one outside the spine and pelvis. Otherwise it is low volume. LATITUDE high risk means at least two of Gleason score ≥8, at least three bone lesions, and measurable visceral metastases. These definitions are not interchangeable, and the original conventional-imaging definitions should not be silently replaced by PSMA PET lesion counts.
rows: Definitive local treatment
Treats the prostate, with selected nodal fields, in a curative plan. ADT can improve outcomes in appropriate risk groups.
It does not imply every patient needs permanent hormone treatment.
Salvage treatment
Treats suspected residual or recurrent local disease after earlier treatment, especially early recurrence after prostatectomy.
A rising PSA should prompt timely review, not an automatic jump to a metastatic drug pathway.
Treating the primary in metastatic disease
STAMPEDE supports prostate radiotherapy in newly diagnosed low-burden metastatic disease.
No overall-survival benefit was demonstrated in the unselected trial population or the high-burden subgroup.
Palliation / urgent local control
Can treat painful bone metastases, bleeding, obstruction or cord compression as part of the appropriate urgent pathway.
Relief at a treated site does not replace systemic cancer control.
Metastasis-directed treatment
Treating selected individual metastases requires specialist multidisciplinary selection, preferably within a trial or prospective programme.
This is a different evidence question from irradiating the prostate itself; limited metastases do not automatically establish a survival benefit.

sections.title: What the pivotal trials actually showed
paragraphs: Overall survival (OS) measures survival from any cause. Metastasis-free survival (MFS) measures time to metastasis or death; it is not the same endpoint. A hazard ratio (HR) compares event rates over follow-up, not the percentage of people cured. The figures below are population results from the stated analyses, not personalised forecasts.
rows: LATITUDE, newly diagnosed high-risk mHSPC, 2017
ADT + abiraterone/prednisone versus ADT + placebos
Supports early intensification in this population; the 17 percentage-point difference is not an individual prediction.
TITAN, mHSPC, 2019
ADT + apalutamide versus ADT + placebo
A different population and follow-up from LATITUDE; not a head-to-head ranking.
ARASENS, mHSPC fit for docetaxel, 2022
ADT + docetaxel + darolutamide versus ADT + docetaxel + placebo
Both groups received docetaxel. This comparison does not answer triplet versus ADT + ARPI doublet.
SPARTAN, high-risk nmCRPC, 2018
Apalutamide + continued ADT versus placebo + ADT
Median MFS 40.5 versus 16.2 months; HR 0.28 (95% CI 0.23–0.35).
Time to metastasis or death, not a 24.3-month guaranteed survival gain.
PROSPER, high-risk nmCRPC, 2020 final OS
Enzalutamide + continued ADT versus placebo + ADT
Median OS 67.0 versus 56.3 months; HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.61–0.89).
Final OS analysis; cannot directly rank against a different drug’s MFS result.
ARAMIS, high-risk nmCRPC, 2019
Darolutamide + continued ADT versus placebo + ADT
Median MFS 40.4 versus 18.4 months; HR 0.41 (95% CI 0.34–0.50).
The NCCP 00693 entry in this batch is nmCRPC; the broader metastatic evidence is a separate setting.
STAMPEDE prostate RT, de novo low-burden metastatic subgroup, 2018
Systemic standard care + prostate RT versus standard care
Prespecified low-burden subgroup. Most participants predated routine modern ARPI intensification.
STAMPEDE high-risk M0 pooled analysis, 2022
ADT with abiraterone-based intensification versus standard care; most planned RT
Selected high-risk population; does not justify escalation in all localised cancer. Adding enzalutamide to abiraterone did not improve MFS and increased toxicity.
EMBARK high-risk biochemical recurrence, 2025 OS analysis
Enzalutamide + leuprolide versus leuprolide
Enzalutamide monotherapy did not show significant OS superiority. This is not the same setting as nmCRPC.

sections.title: Where these five NCCP suites fit
columns: Current NCCP context in this batch
rows: 00103 · Abiraterone + prednisolone
mCRPC after docetaxel, or asymptomatic/mildly symptomatic after ADT failure when chemotherapy is not yet indicated.
Prednisolone 10 mg daily or 5 mg twice daily.
00577 · Abiraterone + prednisolone
Newly diagnosed high-risk mHSPC with ADT.
Prednisolone 5 mg daily. Do not relabel this as every mHSPC or nonmetastatic indication.
00233 · Enzalutamide
NCCP-listed mCRPC settings and high-risk nmCRPC.
Wider EMA/guideline mHSPC and recurrence uses are not automatically included in this NCCP entry.
00574 · Apalutamide
High-risk nmCRPC or mHSPC with ADT.
Each indication has separate eligibility; use the current v5 document.
00693 · Darolutamide
High-risk nmCRPC.
Metastatic doublet/triplet evidence does not extend this particular NCCP entry.

sections.title: The support plan starts with ADT
paragraphs: Explain hot flushes, sexual effects, fatigue, loss of muscle and bone, metabolic changes and mood symptoms. Record a plan for exercise, bone health and cardiometabolic monitoring, and ask directly about sexual function and wellbeing.

Review fracture risk and bone density when starting long-term ADT. Bone treatment for osteoporosis and treatment to prevent metastatic skeletal complications are separate indications. Reconcile all medicines and agree who monitors blood pressure, bloods, symptoms, PSA and testosterone. The selected regimen supplies its own schedule; a general explainer must not invent a universal scan interval.
